'''Salvador Jara Guerrero''' (born 14 October 1955) is a [[Mexicans|Mexican]] philosopher, physicist and professor. He served as Substitute [[Governor of Michoacán]] ([[Institutional Revolutionary Party|PRI]]] beginning on 20 June 2014, following the resignation of [[Fausto Vallejo]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Salvador Jara nuevo gobernador de Michoacán|url=http://www.milenio.com/estados/renuncia_de_Vallejo-sustituto_de_Vallejo-Salvador_Jara-rector_michoacano-nuevo_gobernador_de_Michoacan-Congreso_de_Michoacan_0_320968175.html|accessdate=1 July 2014|agency=Milenio|date=20 June 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Profile|url=http://www.quadratin.com.mx/educativas/Perfil-de-Salvador-Jara/|publisher=Quadratín|accessdate=1 July 2014}}</ref>

Jara Guerrero was rector of the [[Universidad Michoacana de San Nicolás de Hidalgo]] from 2011 until 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=Salvador Jara Guerrero, nuevo rector de la UMSNH|url=http://www.oem.com.mx/elsoldemorelia/Notas/n1916287.htm|accessdate=1 July 2014|publisher=El Sol De Morelia|date=8 January 2011|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304064737/http://www.oem.com.mx/elsoldemorelia/Notas/n1916287.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Salvador Jara once described himself as apolitical, but after his term as governor he became a key member of PRI in Michoacan.<ref name="meta" /> From September 2019 to 2020, he was a member of PRI's Permanent Political Commission of the National Political Council and one of seven national advisors of the National Revolutionary Association "Gral. Leandro Valle".<ref name="meta" /> During the presidency of [[Enrique Peña Nieto]], Jara was an official of the [[Secretariat of Public Education]] (SEP).<ref name="meta" />
